claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
AlCrFeNiSi powder has inherent tendencies toward compositional segregation and residual-stress accumulation during rapid solidification.
An optimized build-platform preheating range may be 400–600 °C for LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed processing is LPBF under an inert atmosphere, with room-temperature mechanical testing and post-fabrication microstructural and residual-stress assessment.
Build-platform preheating will produce a more uniform microstructure with refined and homogenized grain size.
Build-platform preheating will reduce elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
Build-platform preheating will lower defect and porosity density.
Build-platform preheating reduces the temperature gradient between the molten pool and the substrate.
The reduced temperature gradient causes slower and more uniform cooling.
Slower and more uniform cooling decreases residual stresses.
Slower and more uniform cooling limits segregation during solidification and lowers the likelihood of defect formation.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will exhibit statistically significant improvements in tensile strength and ductility relative to the stated baseline.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will show measurable reductions in residual stress and microstructural inhomogeneity relative to the stated baseline.
Room-temperature-substrate LPBF or traditional bulk AlCrFeNiSi components have pronounced segregation, high residual stress, and increased defect density.
Excessive platform preheating may cause unwanted grain growth or other thermal degradation.
The proposed benefit is restricted to additive-manufacturing settings and may not translate directly to conventional casting.
Laser power and scan speed may interact with platform temperature and alter the outcome.
The scalability of platform preheating to larger AlCrFeNiSi builds remains unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The comparison target is inconsistent: the hypothesis refers broadly to conventionally fabricated specimens, the baseline combines room-temperature-substrate LPBF with traditional bulk processing, and the falsification experiment compares preheated LPBF only against room-temperature-substrate LPBF.
